ownership.bus: The ring owns no IMessageBus and calls no handler; a future consumer owns dispatch after dequeue.
ownership.payloadLifetime: Accepted payloads remain in the fixed array until dequeue, reset, or disposal. A producer terminated after slot write but before publication can leave an unpublished payload until later reuse or maintenance.
ownership.managedReferences: Consumed slots are cleared before head publication; reset and disposal clear the array after entered operations drain. Abrupt producer termination can retain an unpublished reference.
ownership.alignment: Managed T[] layout only; no unmanaged arena or alignment promise.
ownership.reclamation: Dequeue clears one slot; reset and disposal clear every slot. Unpublished abandoned slots require reuse, reset, or disposal.

topology.threadAffinity: Exactly one producer and one consumer are required; ownership is a caller precondition and is not dynamically enforced. No Unity API runs in queue operations.
topology.playerLoopPhase: No scheduling is built in; a future consumer must declare its drain phase.

ordering.linearizationPoint: Enqueue publishes the owned tail after payload write; dequeue publishes the owned head after payload read and slot clear. The peer reads its sequence with acquire semantics.

lifecycle.reset: Reset rejects new hot operations, waits for entered operations, atomically discards pending values, clears all slots, resets counters, and returns the dropped count. Concurrent hot calls may receive an InvalidOperationException.
lifecycle.cancellation: Individual accepted items cannot be cancelled; reset drops the whole queue.
lifecycle.disposal: Disposal rejects new work, waits for entered operations, clears all slots, and is idempotent. Maintenance may spin while an entered operation finishes.
lifecycle.exceptions: No user callback runs in an operation. Calls during reset throw InvalidOperationException; calls after disposal throw ObjectDisposedException. Hot paths use Interlocked lifecycle entry and do not wait for capacity.
lifecycle.producerAbandon: No external reservation exists, but abrupt termination between slot write and tail publication can retain an unpublished payload. This unresolved holder blocks production promotion.
lifecycle.partialPublication: The consumer cannot observe a slot before tail publication. Abrupt termination after slot write may leave that slot unpublished until reuse or maintenance.

dynamicDifferences: Queued delivery defers handling and changes synchronous Emit timing; this ring alone has no handler lifecycle, routing, or dispatch-equivalence contract.

decision.workload: Bounded single-producer, single-consumer fixed-ring semantic prototype; compare against the locked control and other queue topologies after #510 calibration and #512 queue timing.
decision.capabilityException: none; no Burst or unmanaged tier is supplied
decision.batchOneOverhead: unmeasured; lifecycle entry adds two atomic operations per hot call
decision.p99: N/A until independent #512 open-loop player sessions support an interval
decision.retainedMemory: slot clearing asserted locally; abrupt producer-abandon retention and GC-retained bytes remain unresolved
decision.playerSize: unmeasured test-only code; no production assembly addition
decision.buildTime: unmeasured test-only code; no production assembly addition
decision.stopRule: Reject on lost, duplicate, reordered, prematurely visible, or retained published payloads. Do not promote with unresolved abrupt-producer retention or without calibrated IL2CPP evidence of at least 20% gain or a supported unique capability.
